summary: Oliver Hellwig works in indology and computational linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and held posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and the University of Zurich (attested 2024–2025).
Oliver Philipp Frey is a scholar in indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he also held an academic post.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was an indologist and philosopher who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).
Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He has held a post as professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen, supervised by Tord Olsson and taught by Karl Harrington Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, and held a post at Lund University.
Olli Littunen specializes in indology and religious studies. Littunen is attested in 2026 as a PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Bisschop.

Om Prakash is a scholar in history, archaeology, and indology who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. Prakash taught at the University of Delhi, Kirori Mal College (attested 1961), and the Delhi School of Economics (attested 2003).

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and Leipzig University (~1912–1915). He later held a post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1939.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and later taught Shenphen Nangwa.

Orna Almogi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Almogi studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at Hamburg, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies and indology scholar who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg. He held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.
Osamu Izumoji (born 1948) is a scholar in sinology who held posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba (1927–2002) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kansai University (~1950–1953), he held posts at Kansai University (~1957–1997), Kogakkan University (~1997), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata (1907–1981) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as head of the art department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

Osborn Bergin (1873–1950) was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, School of Irish Learning, and Freiburg, under Heinrich Zimmer and Kuno Meyer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940–1941).

Oskar von Hinüber (born 1939) is a scholar of indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Mainz under Paul Thieme, and held positions at Mainz (1965–1981) and as professor at the University of Freiburg (1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi (born 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, Panthéon-Sorbonne, and Paris-Sorbonne, and held posts at the CNRS and UC Berkeley.

Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) worked in sinology, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923), the Guimet Museum (1924–1925), and as keeper at the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).
Othmar Frank (1770–1840) was an indologist who studied at the universities of Paris and London. He held professorships at the universities of Bamberg (~1807–1826), Würzburg (1821), and Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka (1903–1989) was an indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930). He later held a professorship at Chuo University from 1949 to 1974.
